config.title: Box Model

intro.title: Box Model
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that visually demonstrates the CSS Box Model by styling a series of boxes. You will learn the core concept of how every HTML element is treated as a rectangular box, consisting of content, padding, border, and margin. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like width, height, padding, border, and margin. By the end, you'll understand how these layers combine to control an element's size and spacing on the page.
intro.usecase: The CSS Box Model is fundamental to every layout you'll create as a developer. When you design a responsive card component for an e-commerce product display, you use padding to create comfortable spacing between the product image and description, borders to visually separate cards, and margins to ensure cards don't touch each other. In dashboard interfaces, you apply these same principles to create properly spaced data panels, form fields with consistent internal padding, and navigation menus with appropriate hover states. Understanding how content, padding, borders, and margins interact allows you to precisely control spacing and alignment in any UI component.

objectives: Apply the box model to configure element dimensions and spacing
Manipulate margin, border, and padding properties to control element layout
Construct responsive layouts by adjusting box model properties
Implement border styles and widths to visually define element boundaries
Configure padding to control internal spacing within elements
Initialize margin adjustments to manage external spacing between elements
Integrate box-sizing property to control total element dimensions

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for the box model demonstration
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure containing a container div and a box div inside it.
steps.hint: Start with the standard HTML5 doctype, then add html, head, and body tags. Inside the body, create a div with class 'container', and inside that, another div with class 'box'.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Box Model Demo</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a container div with a box div inside -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a complete HTML file with the foundational structure needed to demonstrate CSS box model concepts.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a div with class 'container' and inside it a div with class 'box'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the container div and the box div nested inside it with the correct class names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure is incomplete or incorrect. Please create a container div with class 'container' and inside it a box div with class 'box'.

steps.title: Add CSS file and link it to HTML
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file named 'styles.css' and link it to the HTML file by adding a link tag in the head section.
steps.hint: Use the <link> tag with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css' inside the <head> element.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Linking a CSS file -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Box Model Demo</title>
    <!-- Add link tag here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add a container div with a box div inside -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file will have a link to an external CSS file, enabling styling of the box model demonstration.
successCriteria: A link tag with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css' is added inside the head section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the link tag might be missing or have incorrect attributes. Ensure it has rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The link tag is not correctly added. Please add <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> inside the head section.

steps.title: Style the container with basic layout properties
steps.instruction: In your CSS file, add a CSS rule for the container div that sets display: flex, justify-content: center, align-items: center, and height: 100vh.
steps.hint: Create a CSS selector for the container div and apply the specified properties to create a centered flex container that fills the viewport height.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will become a flex container that centers its child both horizontally and vertically, and fills the full viewport height.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for the container div with display: flex, justify-content: center, align-items: center, and height: 100vh.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your CSS rule includes all four required properties: display: flex, justify-content: center, align-items: center, and height: 100vh.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule doesn't match the requirements. Check that you're targeting the container div and applying all four layout properties.

steps.title: Apply width and height to the box element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .box class to set its width to 200px and height to 150px.
steps.hint: Use the width and height properties with pixel values to define the content area dimensions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The box element will have a defined content area of 200 pixels wide by 150 pixels tall.
successCriteria: The .box selector has width: 200px; and height: 150px; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both width and height properties with the correct pixel values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The box element doesn't have the required width and height properties. Check the CSS rule for .box.

steps.title: Add padding to create space inside the box
steps.instruction: Add a padding property to the .box selector to create space between the content and the border.
steps.hint: Use the padding property with a value like 20px to add space inside the box.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box selector now includes a padding property, creating visible space inside the box.
successCriteria: The .box selector has a padding property with a valid value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the padding property correctly to the .box selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The padding property is missing or incorrect. Try adding padding: 20px; to the .box selector.

steps.title: Add a border around the box
steps.instruction: Add a border to the .box class by specifying border-width, border-style, and border-color properties.
steps.hint: Use the border shorthand property or specify individual border properties like border-width, border-style, and border-color.
steps.expectedOutcome: The box element will have a visible border around its edges, demonstrating the border area of the box model.
successCriteria: The .box class includes border properties (width, style, color) that create a visible border.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some border properties, but make sure to include all three: width, style, and color for a complete border.
steps.feedbackWrong: The border isn't properly defined. Check that you've added border properties to the .box class with valid values.

steps.title: Add margin to create space outside the box
steps.instruction: Add a margin property to the .box selector to create space outside the border. Use a value like 30px.
steps.hint: The margin property adds space outside an element's border, separating it from other elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box selector now has a margin property applied, creating space outside its border.
successCriteria: The .box selector includes a margin property with a pixel value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a margin property to the .box selector with a pixel value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box selector should include a margin property. Try adding 'margin: 30px;' or similar.

steps.title: Add background color to visualize the content area
steps.instruction: Add a background-color property to the .box selector to make the content area visually distinct from the padding area.
steps.hint: Use a CSS color value like a named color (e.g., 'lightblue'), hex code, or rgb() function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule now includes a background-color property, making the content area visually distinct.
successCriteria: The .box selector has a background-color property with a valid CSS color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but make sure it's background-color with a valid color value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box selector should have a background-color property with a color value.

steps.title: Add box-sizing: border-box to see the difference
steps.instruction: Add the box-sizing property with the value border-box to the .box rule to see how it affects total width and height calculations.
steps.hint: The box-sizing property controls how width and height are calculated. Use border-box to include padding and border in the element's total dimensions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box rule now includes box-sizing: border-box, which will make the element's total width and height include padding and border instead of adding them to the specified dimensions.
successCriteria: The .box rule contains the property box-sizing with the value border-box.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added box-sizing: border-box to the .box rule. Make sure the property name and value are spelled correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The box-sizing property with value border-box is not present in the .box rule. Try adding it to see how it affects the box model calculations.

steps.title: Add text content and style it to complete the demonstration
steps.instruction: Add a text color property to the .box selector to style the text content inside the box.
steps.hint: Use the color property with a value like a named color (e.g., 'white') or a hex code (e.g., '#333').
steps.expectedOutcome: The text inside the box will have visible styling, completing the box model demonstration.
successCriteria: The .box selector includes a color property with a valid CSS color value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a color property to the .box selector with a valid color value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box selector doesn't have a color property yet. Add one to style the text content.
